EXECUTIVE SUMMARY: This Zone Change request hasbeen submitted in order to facilitate
a parkinglot expansion for Wyoming Bank and Trust, which recently completed an expansion of
fromMR-2Medium Density Residential-Developing to CB Community Business.If
approved, this request will bring thelot under the same zoning requirements as the rest ofthe site
to the west.Further development of the lot projectwill require a Site Plan Review for theentire
site, at which time the parking, landscaping, accesses and other design requirements will be
evaluated for compliance.
ZONE CHANGE DATA: In reviewing, providing comments, and making recommendations
and decisions on a proposed preliminary plat, the Staff, Planning Commission and City Council
shall use the following criteria:
PLAN CHEYENNE.The application is in accordance with the development policies and physical
patterns identified in the Comprehensive Plan.
The Future Land Use Plan recommends Mixed-Use Commercial Emphasis for this area (see
attached aerial map).The Mixed-Use Commercial category is intended to promote a range of
land uses, with primarily retail, office, light industrial, and live/work designed as an“activity
center".Parks, plazas and/or open space should also be part of the core of Mixed-Use
Commercial areas.Apartments and townhomes and other residential uses are also encouraged as
part of the mix of uses.Places of worship and other public or civic uses are also appropriate.
The site is also located very near to an area identified as a Mixed-use Commercial Activity
Center.As such, CB Community Business is an appropriate underlying zone district as
recommended.
SURROUNDING AREA.The application is compatible with nearby property，specifically
considering existing zoning the Comprehensive Plan, and any other official plans and policies
created under the guidance of that plan for these areas.
Thisis an established neighborhood with along history of both commercial and residential
Page3, Zone Change Request/UDC-13-00205, KGH-Z
4:
development.As Cheyenne has grown, the commercial businesses along Yellowstone have
expanded.Such is the case with Wyoming Bank and Trust, the applicant in this request.The lot
directly to the south ofthis one, across Kornegay, iszoned CB and is currently occupied bya
custom picture framing and retail business.Also existing along Korn egay are a veterinary clinic,
construction business and warehouse(Siding Specialists), a picture-framing shop, and an
educational facility operated by Stride Learning Center.It is typically desirable to have similar
uses facing each other across a street, with use transitions occurring mid-block(e.g., across an
alley).
ZONING, BASIC STANDARDs&Us Es.The suitability of the subject property for development
according to the standards and uses of the existing zoning district, compared to the suitability of
the subject property for development according to the standards and uses of the proposed zoning
district;
This Zone Change enables the lot to become more integrated with the rest ofthebank site, which
is zoned CB.In general, it is not good practice to have two or more zone districts on a single,
integrated site.While parking lots are allowed in anMR-2District, they are subject to different
regulation and design requirements.Furthermore, if the lot remains MR-2, it will not be subject
to the required 15’landscape strip between a CB and MR-2 district, which in this case will
provide a buffer to the lower density development to the north and east (ref.Table 6-10, UDC).
STREETS&OPENSPACE.The ability of thesubject property and surrounding vicinity tobe
developed according to the Subdivision Standards in Article4considering the proposed zoning;
This Zone Change request will not preclude the area from further development according to the
standards laid out in Article 4.Lot access is currently onto Kornegay Court, a local road, and
the surrounding street network is well established. The block perimeter requirements are met
(and do not change). Sidewalk, curb, and gutter will be required and built to current City
standards. The site also appears to be within a quarter of a mile from the Greenway.
ZONING, INTENT, APPLICABILITY&DESIGN OBJECTIVES.The ability of the application to support
the Intent and Applicability statements of the proposed zoning district, and achieve the Design
Objectives of any specific standards.
The CBDistrict is intended for Retail, Employment, Service and Civic uses that may serve a
number of residential neighborhoods or other districts in meeting daily needs, discretionary
needs, or other business functions.The district regulations are designed to encourage these uses,
while also protecting the abutting and nearby areas, such as a required 15’landscaped buffer
between this lot and the surrounding MR-2Lots to the north and east.This district should
employ a well-connected internal network to facilitate a park once, walkable atmosphere and
good internal circulation, and transitions to adjacent areas should be designed to minimize
impacts on surrounding areas and transportation networks.

This zone district is intended for commercial use, such as the expansion of off-street parking and
internal circulation being proposed with this application.The proposal is also adjacent to the
commercial activity along Yellowstone and along Kornegay to the west and south.Thelocation
of this zone district is consistent with the intent, applicability and context described in the zone
district (ref. 5.4.2.a-c, UDC). The proposal is located in an area with an established
transportation network to accommodate it.
ZONING, FUTURE DEVELOPMENT.The ability of all potential future development to meet all
applicable standards for development in the proposed zoning district, including other
development options in the event that any specific development proposed in association with the
application is not executed after approval.
It is anticipated that the parking lot expansion will take place in the very near future. However,
should the expansion not materialize, and the CBzoning is in place, thislot will still have a few
options should the proposed project not materialize, although a residential use will not be one of
them.If it is developed without integration with the site to the west, the relatively small size of
the lot will constrain the intensity of the use.

BE IT ORDAINED BY THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE, WYOMING:
Section 1. That the owner of the property described herein, has applied for a zoning map
amendment (*zone change")for said property in accordance with Section 2.2.1, Zoning Map
Amendment, of the Cheyenne Unified Development Code ("UDC").
Section 2.That on July 1, 2013, the City of Cheyenne Planning Commission conducted a public
hearing, reviewed the proposed zone change that is the subject of this ordinance, and recommended
approval of said zone change.
Section 3.That the Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne finds that the zone change that is
the subject of this ordinance meets the criteria specified in Section 2.2.1.d of the UDC.
Section 4. That, in accordance with Section 2.2.1, Zoning Map Amendment, Section 5.1.2,
Zoning Districts Established, and Section 5.1.3, Official Zoning Map, of the UDC, the aforementioned
Block 1, Kornegay Homesites, 2nd Filing, Cheyenne, Wyoming, is hereby changed to CB Community
Business.
Section5. That the City Engineer is hereby authorized and directed to alter and amend the
Official Zoning Map as described in 5.1.3 of the UDC to comply with the zone change as described in
Section 4 above when this ordinance takes effect in accordance with Section 7 below.
